Datasection.why: operates AI data centres and sells NVIDIA GPU server capacity (GPU cloud) to AI infrastructure customers, so its revenue rises with AI compute demand
Datasection.evidence: Datasection TDnet 09-18-2026: large order from a US-based AI infrastructure company for usage capacity on NVIDIA GPU servers at its planned AI data centre, USD 175.2 million per year

players.product: GPU cloud capacity: usage allocations on NVIDIA GPU servers in the AI data centres it operates

quarterly_data.signal: Large order (announced 09-18-2026): an unnamed US-based AI infrastructure company serving enterprise customers ordered the provision of usage capacity on NVIDIA GPU servers at an AI data centre the group plans to open. Order value USD 175.2 million per year (USD 525.6 million over 3 years, USD 876 million over 5 years); contract term 3 years, extendable by up to 2 years at the customer's option; phased provision from October 2026 with the full capacity planned for November or December 2026. The customer is not disclosed at its request and has no capital, personnel or other business relationship with the company; the data-centre location and the NVIDIA GPU model and quantity are also undisclosed. The order becomes effective on the customer's initial deposit, due by 09-25-2026.
quarterly_data.figure: USD 175.2 million per year; USD 525.6 million over 3 years; USD 876 million over 5 years

quarterly_data.signal: Outlook: the project is already included in the FY ending March 2027 consolidated forecast. Provision starts later than the phased start (July 2026) assumed in that forecast, but the contract unit price is above the assumed price, so the company expects this project's current-year revenue to be lower than first expected and its profit higher; it will disclose promptly if the forecast needs revision.
